HOME SCIENCE MARCH — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #12
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: HOME SCIENCE MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Meals for Special Occasions? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Meals for Special Occasions.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Meals for Special Occasions.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Meals for Special Occasions.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Meals for Special Occasions.

7. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Primary consumers only

8. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 100 °C

16. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. watt (W)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

17. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

18. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Overgrazing continuously

19. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

20. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)

   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
